# Java Edition protocol/FAQ

> Minecraft Java snapshot: `1.21.8`  
> Protocol version: `772`  
> Source: [Java Edition protocol/FAQ](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/FAQ?oldid=3158616)

People very, very often have questions regarding the [*Java Edition* protocol](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol "Java Edition protocol"), so we'll try to address some of the most common ones on this document. If you're still having trouble, join us on the [Minecraft Wiki's Discord server](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Wiki:Discord "Minecraft Wiki:Discord"), the [Minecraft Protocol Discord server](https://discord.gg/Tf4xwK3Ke7), or our IRC channel [#mcdevs on irc.libera.chat](ircs://irc.libera.chat:6697/mcdevs).

## Is the protocol documentation complete?

Depending on your definition, *yes*! All packet types are known and their layout documented. Some finer details are missing, but everything you need to make functional programs is present. We also collect information on the [pre-release protocol](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Development_version "Java Edition protocol/Development version") changes, allowing us to quickly document new releases.

## What's the normal login sequence for a client?

(This is about joining a Minecraft server. See [Microsoft authentication](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Microsoft_authentication "Microsoft authentication") for how to log in to a Minecraft account, and [protocol encryption](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Protocol_encryption "Protocol encryption") for details on player authentication during server login.)

The recommended login sequence as of 1.21 looks like this, where **C** is the client and **S** is the server:

1. Client connects to the server
2. **C**→**S**: [Handshake](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Handshake "Java Edition protocol/Packets") State=2
3. **C**→**S**: [Login Start](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Login_Start "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
4. **S**→**C**: [Encryption Request](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Encryption_Request "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (optional)
5. Client auth (Only if server sent Encryption Request)
6. **C**→**S**: [Encryption Response](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Encryption_Response "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Only if server sent Encryption Request)
7. Server auth, both enable encryption (Only if server sent Encryption Request)
8. **S** → **C**: [Set Compression](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Set_Compression "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Optional, enables compression)
9. **S** → **C**: [Login Success](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Login_Success "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
10. **C** → **S**: [Login Acknowledged](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Login_Acknowledged "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
11. **C** → **S**: [Serverbound Plugin Message](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Serverbound_Plugin_Message_(configuration) "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Optional, [`minecraft:brand`](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Plugin_channel?action=edit&redlink=1 "Plugin channel (page does not exist)") with the client's brand)
12. **C** → **S**: [Client Information](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Client_Information_(configuration) "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Optional)
13. **S** → **C**: [Clientbound Plugin Message](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Clientbound_Plugin_Message_(configuration) "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Optional, [`minecraft:brand`](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Plugin_channel?action=edit&redlink=1 "Plugin channel (page does not exist)") with the server's brand)
14. **S** → **C**: [Feature Flags](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Feature_Flags "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Optional)
15. **S** → **C**: [Clientbound Known Packs](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Clientbound_Known_Packs "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
16. **C** → **S**: [Serverbound Known Packs](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Serverbound_Known_Packs "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
17. **S** → **C**: [Registry Data](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Registry_Data_2 "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Multiple)
18. **S** → **C**: [Update Tags](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Update_Tags_(configuration) "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Optional)
19. **S** → **C**: [Finish Configuration](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Finish_Configuration "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
20. **C** → **S**: [Acknowledge Finish Configuration](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Acknowledge_Finish_Configuration "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
21. **S** → **C**: [Login (play)](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Login_(play) "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
22. **S** → **C**: [Change Difficulty](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Change_Difficulty "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Optional)
23. **S** → **C**: [Player Abilities](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Player_Abilities_(clientbound) "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Optional)
24. **S** → **C**: [Set Held Item](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Set_Held_Item_(clientbound) "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Optional)
25. **S** → **C**: [Update Recipes](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Update_Recipes "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Optional)
26. **S** → **C**: [Entity Event](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Entity_Event "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Optional, for the [OP permission level](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Server.properties#op-permission-level "Server.properties"); see [Entity statuses#Player](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Wiki:Projects/wiki.vg_merge/Entity_statuses#Player "Minecraft Wiki:Projects/wiki.vg merge/Entity statuses"))
27. **S** → **C**: [Commands](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Commands "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Optional)
28. **S** → **C**: [Update Recipe Book](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Update_Recipe_Book "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Optional)
29. **S** → **C**: [Synchronize Player Position](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Synchronize_Player_Position "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
30. **C** → **S**: [Confirm Teleportation](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Confirm_Teleportation "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
31. **C** → **S**: [Set Player Position and Rotation](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Set_Player_Position_and_Rotation "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Optional, to confirm the spawn position)
32. **S** → **C**: [Server Data](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Server_Data "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Optional)
33. **S** → **C**: [Player Info Update](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Player_Info_Update "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Add Player action, all players except the one joining (the vanilla server separates these, you don't need to))
34. **S** → **C**: [Player Info Update](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Player_Info_Update "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Add Player action, joining player)
35. **S** → **C**: [Initialize World Border](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Initialize_World_Border "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Optional)
36. **S** → **C**: [Update Time](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Update_Time "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Optional)
37. **S** → **C**: [Set Default Spawn Position](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Set_Default_Spawn_Position "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Optional, “home” spawn, not where the client will spawn on login)
38. **S** → **C**: [Game Event](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Game_Event "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Start waiting for level chunks event, required for the client to spawn. Despite the name, a custom server may choose to send some chunks before sending this packet)
39. **S** → **C**: [Set Ticking State](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Set_Ticking_State "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Optional)
40. **S** → **C**: [Step Tick](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Step_Tick "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (Optional, the vanilla server sends this regardless of ticking state)
41. **S** → **C**: [Set Center Chunk](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Set_Center_Chunk "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
42. **S** → **C**: [Chunk Data and Update Light](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Chunk_Data_and_Update_Light "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (One sent for each chunk in a circular area centered on the player's position)
43. **C** → **S**: [Player Loaded](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Player_Loaded "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (After the "Loading terrain..." screen has closed (see [below](https://minecraft.wiki#…my_player_isn't_spawning!)), or skipped if 60 ticks pass before then)
44. **S** → **C**: inventory, entities, etc.

### Offline mode

If the vanilla server is in offline mode, it will not send the [Encryption Request](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Encryption_Request "Java Edition protocol/Packets") packet, and likewise, the client should not send [Encryption Response](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Encryption_Response "Java Edition protocol/Packets"). In this case, encryption is never enabled, and no authentication is performed.

Clients can tell that a server is in offline mode if the server sends a [Login Success](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Login_Success "Java Edition protocol/Packets") without sending [Encryption Request](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Encryption_Request "Java Edition protocol/Packets").

Versions 1.20.5 and newer support protocol encryption in offline mode, in which case the [Encryption Request](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Encryption_Request "Java Edition protocol/Packets") packet can be sent with Should Authenticate set to false, and both the client and server should not authenticate with Mojang. However, it's currently not possible to configure the vanilla server to do this.

## What does the normal status ping sequence look like?

When a vanilla client and server exchange information in a status ping, the exchange of packets will be as follows:

1. **C** → **S**: [Handshake](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Handshake "Java Edition protocol/Packets") with Next State set to 1 ([Status](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Status "Java Edition protocol/Packets"))
2. Client and Server set protocol state to [Status](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Status "Java Edition protocol/Packets").
3. **C** → **S**: [Status Request](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Status_Request "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
4. **S** → **C**: [Status Response](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Status_Response "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
5. **C** → **S**: [Ping Request](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Ping_Request_(status) "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
6. **S** → **C**: [Pong Response](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Pong_Response_(status) "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
7. Both sides close the connection

(Note that **C** is the vanilla client and **S** is the vanilla server).

The [Ping Request](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Ping_Request_(status) "Java Edition protocol/Packets") packet may be left out, however the client will not receive a [Pong Response](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Pong_Response_(status) "Java Edition protocol/Packets") packet and the server won't close the connection.

## I think I've done everything right, but…

### …my player isn't spawning!

The Minecraft client will wait at the "Loading Terrain..." screen until late in the login sequence. As of 1.21.4 (and starting with 1.20.3), in order for the client to spawn, it must have received a [Game Event](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Game_Event "Java Edition protocol/Packets") packet with event 13 ("Start waiting for level chunks"), and at least one of the following conditions must be met:

- The player is in a loaded chunk (sent via [Chunk Data and Update Light](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Chunk_Data_and_Update_Light "Java Edition protocol/Packets")).
- The player is below the minimum world height or above the maximum world height (teleported via [Synchronize Player Position](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Synchronize_Player_Position "Java Edition protocol/Packets")).
- The player is in spectator mode (set via [Player Info Update](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Player_Info_Update "Java Edition protocol/Packets"), *not* the Game Mode field in Login (play)!)
- The player is dead (set via [Set Health](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Set_Health "Java Edition protocol/Packets") or [Combat Death](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Combat_Death "Java Edition protocol/Packets")).

The client will also spawn after spending 30 seconds in the loading screen, even if it never received Game Event 13.

In past versions, you could either (1.19.3 through 1.20.2) send the default spawn position packet or (pre-1.19.3) send the player position packet. In general, try sending packets that inform the client about the player's position in the world in order to get past the loading terrain screen.

In version 1.21, it became required to send the known packs packet with `minecraft:core` version `1.21`.

As of 1.21.4, the minimum packets that need to be received and sent by the server in order to get the client past the loading terrain screen and into the world appear to be:

1. Receive [Handshake](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Handshake "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
2. Receive [Login Start](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Login_Start "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
3. Send [Login Success](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Login_Success "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
4. Receive [Login Acknowledged](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Login_Acknowledged "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
5. Send [Clientbound Known Packs](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Clientbound_Known_Packs "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
6. Receive [Serverbound Known Packs](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Serverbound_Known_Packs "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
7. Send multiple [Registry Data](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Registry_Data "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
8. Send [Finish Configuration](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Finish_Configuration "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
9. Receive [Acknowledge Finish Configuration](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Acknowledge_Finish_Configuration "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
10. Send [Login (Play)](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Login_.28play.29 "Java Edition protocol/Packets")
11. Send [Game Event](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Game_Event "Java Edition protocol/Packets"), Start waiting for level chunks
12. Send [Chunk Data and Update Light](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Chunk_Data_and_Update_Light "Java Edition protocol/Packets") and/or [Synchronize Player Position](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Synchronize_Player_Position "Java Edition protocol/Packets") (see above)

The most difficult part of this may be sending any necessary NBTs in the [Registry Data](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol#Registry_Data "Java Edition protocol") packet. Note that if you tell the vanilla client you have 0 known packs, it will blatantly lie to you, so you will probably need to record one from the standard server and replay it. Or you can find someone who has done that already, for example in [Norbiros' gist](https://gist.github.com/Norbiros/f604ce46821e68c50260a169a9921560). You can also find JSON representation of this packet in [PrismarineJS/minecraft-data repo on GitHub](https://github.com/PrismarineJS/minecraft-data/blob/master/data/pc/1.20.2/loginPacket.json).

### …chunks are randomly showing and disappearing!

The vanilla client only reliably renders chunks surrounded by other loaded chunks on all sides. See [Chunk Format#Tips and notes](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Wiki:Projects/wiki.vg_merge/Chunk_Format#Tips_and_notes "Minecraft Wiki:Projects/wiki.vg merge/Chunk Format").

### …the client is trying to send an invalid packet that begins with 0xFE01

The client is attempting a [legacy ping](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Wiki:Projects/wiki.vg_merge/Server_List_Ping#1.6 "Minecraft Wiki:Projects/wiki.vg merge/Server List Ping"), this happens if your server did not respond to the [Server List Ping](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Minecraft_Wiki:Projects/wiki.vg_merge/Server_List_Ping "Minecraft Wiki:Projects/wiki.vg merge/Server List Ping") properly, including if it sent malformed JSON.

### …the client disconnects after some time with a "Timed out" error

The server is expected to send a [Keep Alive](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Java_Edition_protocol/Packets#Keep_Alive_(clientbound) "Java Edition protocol/Packets") packet every 1-15 seconds (if the server does not send a keep alive within 20 seconds of state change to Play, the client will disconnect from the server for **Timed Out**), and the client should respond with the serverbound version of that packet. If either party does not receive keep alives for some period of time, they will disconnect.

### ...some of the packets I expect to receive seem to be missing or too short

You may be misusing the socket API. In particular, it is invalid to assume that the amount of data returned by calls to `recv` (or equivalent, depending on the API you're using) relates to packet boundaries in any way. There are no "borders" in a [TCP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transmission_Control_Protocol "wikipedia:Transmission Control Protocol") data stream, only bytes. Regardless of how any two consecutive packets are sent, the receiver may get one packet, then the other, both at once, half of one, then the rest of both, or any other permutation of buffer sizes adding up to the total size of the packets. The only correct way to know where one packet ends and another begins is the packet length field, and you need to be prepared to handle multiple packets in one buffer, packets split across multiple buffers, etc. (as well as length fields split across multiple buffers!)

Similarly, depending on the API being used, a `send` call may also not guarantee that its whole input buffer is sent (consult the relevant documentation for details). This may also cause the connection to appear to hang during the login process, since the server will be left waiting indefinitely for the rest of the packet to arrive.

One reason why packets sent separately may arrive at once is [Nagle's algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nagle%27s_algorithm "wikipedia:Nagle's algorithm"), a feature of many TCP implementations intended to improve efficiency particularly for applications making lots of small `send` calls. It is not the *only* reason, though, and disabling it should not be seen as a solution to the problem discussed here. Nonetheless, the delays it introduces are detrimental to real-time applications like Minecraft, so the vanilla client and server disable it, and you should too. This is typically done by enabling a socket option called `TCP_NODELAY`. Especially when disabling Nagle's algorithm, you should group multiple packets sent during the same tick in one send buffer for the best performance.
